title: Season 2, Ep 5: Agent SDK standardization
oneliner: Standardize how agents get built: an agent SDK gives every team the same standards, documentation, procedures, and best practices - Claude's agent SDK being one to adapt.
says: As a platform solution architect you have standardized the MCP hub and the centralized prompt registry across LOBs. Now focus on the agent SDK: it provides the standards, documentation, procedures, and best practices for implementing agent solutions in your organization. Every organization can have its own agent SDK standards - Claude has the Claude Agent SDK, and other organizations can take such standard SDKs and customize them for their needs.
explained: The pattern being standardized away: every team hand-rolls its own agent loop - its own tool-calling code, retry logic, memory handling, tracing. Six teams, six subtly broken agent frameworks. A standard SDK makes the correct way the easy way: one implementation of the hard parts, with guardrails and observability built in, so application teams write business logic instead of plumbing.

His point about customization is the architect's move: you rarely write an SDK from zero. You take a proven one - he names Claude's - and wrap it in your organization's policies: which tools agents may call, what they must log, which models they default to. The SDK then becomes the enforcement point for everything else this season builds - the MCP hub, the prompt registry, the evaluation pipeline all plug into it.
takeaway: Don't let every team invent its own agent loop: adopt a proven agent SDK, wrap it in your policies, and make it the one approved path.
